items.title: Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Sparks Theories About 2 Doctor Dooms as Fans Hope for a Surprise Cameo from Cillian Murphy
items.description: The new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is here, and some fans believe it has a few clues that suggest the film is hiding two Doctor Dooms – and maybe even a cameo from Cillian Murphy.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The new Avengers: Doomsday trailer is here, and some fans believe it has a few clues that suggest the film is hiding two Doctor Dooms – and maybe even a cameo from Cillian Murphy.

Warning! Potential spoilers for Avengers: Doomsday follow.

Marvel Studios has seemingly been pretty forthcoming when it comes to the cast for this year's new Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) movie. Of the long lineup of A-listers on the call sheet are faces from the X-Men, Fantastic Four, and more, but the casting choice that has remained controversial among fans since its announcement is Iron Man actor Robert Downey Jr. as Victor von Doom.

The few Avengers: Doomsday clips we've seen thus far have revealed the hero-turned-villain star's in-costume look – or have they? That's the question fans have been asking since the team-up film's new trailer arrived as part of D23 2026. With tens of millions of viewers in just a few days, it's clear the video has something to offer ahead of the full premiere in December, but some believe it's hiding a few clues about Doctor Doom duplicates, too.

"All of you have lived stolen lives," he can be heard saying in between shots of a screaming Reed Richards played by Pedro Pascal. "But now you must give them back."

Where past sneak peeks for the movie haven't dived too far down the Victor von Doom rabbit hole, the D23 trailer is really more about him than any of Earth's Mightiest Heroes. It starts with Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm talking about the Latverian leader as someone who "used to be kind" and "caring" before we then see him toss Thor like an ant and raise an army of sentinels. Although he certainly seems to present an Avengers-level threat that could rival Thanos, the conversation surrounding his identity lies in the details.

A few close-ups of the magic-powered villain's eyes are all we really get when it comes to glimpses of what's behind his metal mask, but that's all fans online needed to stir up conversation. You see, this character has bluish-green eyes, while Downey Jr.'s are brown. This Doctor Doom also has a small mole next to one of his eyes, where the actor believed to be playing him does not.

Clearly there are 2 Dooms with RDJ being the fake doom https://t.co/g3okvI7hmH

— Suki 💅 (@_SuksTeR_) August 15, 2026

"One looks blue. The other video looks brown," one fan speculated after the trailer was released. "Is there more than one Doom?"

"I think there will be two Dooms," another said. "The real Doom, and a Tony variant."

The idea, then, is that the Doom we've seen here is a different one from the Doom Downey Jr. is playing. If these are truly our first signs that Avengers: Doomsday features more than one Doctor Doom, then the next logical question is 'Who is playing the other one?' Many online believe Murphy, who is best known for starring in movies like Oppenheimer and 28 Years Later, makes the most sense. He was a popular fancast pick as Marvel put the new Avengers movie together behind the scenes early on. He also happens to have much lighter eyes.

Cillian Murphy speaking Romanian and Romani 👀 Could he be the real Doctor Doom? 🤯#AvengersDoomsday pic.twitter.com/JLVGubmJTA

— BLURAYANGEL 🦇 (@blurayangel) August 16, 2026

If the rumors about Cillian Murphy actually playing the real Doctor Doom are true…

is this a casting upgrade or downgrade?👀#AvengersDoomsday pic.twitter.com/YQm5JJ9SEm

— Echo ↬ (@vikku60879) August 16, 2026

If this is true, I bet I know who the other Dr. Doom is. https://t.co/SovOL6rxL1 pic.twitter.com/pmHwjRmpnp

— Comics Explained (@comicsexplained) August 15, 2026

Many believe Downey Jr. could be playing a good-guy version of the character, leaving the evil one to be played by Murphy or even someone else. Other theories rattling around social media feeds have revolved around a surprise return for Michael Fassbender's Magneto, an alternate Reed Richards, or, if Marvel is feeling really daring, Chris Evans' Steve Rogers.

This is all proof that a mystery actor is playing Doom and not the former Iron Man star, right?! Well, no. As others have pointed out, that mole might seem a bit strange, but some combination of movie magic and special contact lenses could easily explain away these discrepancies. That's done little to stop the theories from spinning on.

"This is literally just RDJ with colored contacts y’all overthinking it lol," one fan argued.

"lmao they are not paying RDJ multi millions to play a fake Doom," another teased.

"Why not? They paid Ben Kingsley millions to play a fake Mandarin," another user replied.

Meanwhile, the appearance of a second, new costume for Victor von Doom that popped up at D23 has helped fuel the Avengers: Doomsday theory fire through the weekend. Some blink-and-you'll-miss-it moments in the trailer also show what appears to be a smoother, less angry mask design and a more simplistic suit. It does seem odd that the big bad guy would care enough about his fashion to have slightly different outfits for specific occasions.

Even then, though, we already knew Doom would be switching his clothes. The costume and mask featured in most promotional material is already quite different from what we saw at the end of last year's The Fantastic Four: First Steps. The reasoning behind the change is unclear, with some suspecting one might be for fighting off superheroes, while the other is used when Doom wants to favor more peaceful methods.

Doctor Doom is wearing his two different costumes in the same scene pic.twitter.com/2DjTt8dosr

— Marvel Perfect Gifs & Clips (@MCUPerfectGifs) August 15, 2026

🚨 This theory proves there are two Doctor Dooms in Avengers: Doomsday

When Doctor Doom is thrown from that tower-like structure, he changes his outfit mid-air and lands wearing a suit that looks less armored.

But later, when he is seen fighting Thor, you can see the same… pic.twitter.com/pJufmcWZdp

— Marvel Decoded (@MarvelDecoded) August 15, 2026

Regardless of whichever side of the theory fence you fall on, it's hard to blame the fans of a cinematic movie universe that has reveled in multiversal shenanigans for the last seven years. Character variants have, quite famously, occupied the same screen more than a few times. If Spider-Man did it, Doctor Doom can too, right?

It's certainly possible, but there is much, much more MCU to watch before we get all of the answers. Avengers: Doomsday will pull back its green curtain to clear up many of its mysteries when it premieres December 18, 2026, but it's far from the end. The film will then lead directly into Avengers: Secret Wars, which won't arrive until another year later, come December 17, 2027.

So, will there be two Doctor Dooms? Is Downey Jr.'s character the movie's villain or its hero? Will Iron Man come back from the dead? We'll have to wait to find out. Until then, you can see how Marvel announced the first batch of cast members for its new X-Men movie. You can also check out the new trailer for the upcoming MCU TV show, VisionQuest. Finally, be sure to catch up on all of the biggest D23 news from the Disney Entertainment Showcase right here.

items.title: Simu Liu Says Sleeping Dogs Movie Has 'a REAL Path Forward' Amid Dealmaking With Square Enix
items.description: Marvel star Simu Liu has offered a positive update on his long-in-development Sleeping Dogs movie adaptation, saying the film has "a REAL path forward" as discussions with game publisher Square Enix continue.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Marvel star Simu Liu has offered a positive update on his long-in-development Sleeping Dogs movie adaptation, saying the film has "a REAL path forward" as discussions with game publisher Square Enix continue.

The Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings actor offered a treat to patient fans when asked about the project's status on X/Twitter. It's been some time since we heard where Sleeping Dogs was at, but don't worry, Liu said it is still very much in the works.

"Okay, here it is," he replied to a fan asking for an update. "We’re moving along really well, we have a director, and a production company, and a REAL path forward."

okay, here it is. we’re moving along really well, we have a director, and a production company, and a REAL path forward.

we’re just in the dealmaking process with the game studio rn (which is a total fan moment for me bc i love SquareEnix). your support is fuelling us all! https://t.co/1ufLYZab0E

— Simu Liu (@SimuLiu) August 16, 2026

Liu quickly stepped in to announce he had taken the reins to develop a movie based on Square Enix and United Front Games' Grand Theft Auto-inspired crime drama after Donnie Yen confirmed his take had been canned in early 2025. Although the nature of his involvement was initially kept a mystery, IGN reported that a Sleeping Dogs movie was, in fact, in development, with Liu set to produce and star as a live-action version of main character Wei Shen.

The star's new update also mentions a director, which was confirmed to be Nobody 2 and Killers filmmaker Timo Tjahjanto late last year. Video game adaptation veteran studio Story Kitchen is also in the mix, and in October 2025, Liu announced that the Sleeping Dogs script draft was completed.

Although things are moving slowly, they are absolutely still moving. Liu and the rest of the Sleeping Dogs team now need to work with Square Enix if they want to get the ball rolling toward an eventual release.

"We’re just in the dealmaking process with the game studio [right now] (which is a total fan moment for me [because] I love Square Enix)," he added. "Your support is fueling us all!"

"Set in a vibrant, contemporary, neon-infused neo-noir Hong Kong," an official description on the Story Kitchen website says. "WEI SHEN is an undercover cop torn between his duty as an officer of the law and, separately, his loyalty to a family of violent Triads that he’s trying to infiltrate, many of whom he grew up with on the streets."

The Sleeping Dogs movie currently has no firm release date or window. Liu has plenty to keep him busy in the meantime, as he's set to return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe in Avengers: Doomsday this December. He's also still pushing to make Shang-Chi 2 happen. Until we learn more, you can read IGN's review of the 2012 game to find out why we thought it deserved an 8.5/10.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Becomes First Spider-Man Movie to Reach $2 Billion in Theaters
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has officially crossed $2 billion at the global box office, marking the first time Marvel's wall-crawling hero has ever reached the theatrical landmark.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day has officially crossed $2 billion at the global box office, marking the first time Marvel's wall-crawling hero has ever reached the theatrical landmark.

The new Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) flick passed the milestone after premiering in theaters July 31, 2026, a little more than three weeks ago. It's a spectacular achievement, with the box office split breaking down to an estimated $785.8 million domestically and $1.236 billion internationally.

Star Tom Holland and director Destin Daniel Cretton's Brand New Day now stands as Sony's highest-grossing release ever at a whopping $2.022 billion. Reaching the big $2b makes it the eighth film to do so, but despite some tremendous past successes under his belt, it's a first for Spider-Man.

Spider-Man: No Way Home came close to reaching the number upon its premiere in 2021, with its total climbing to $1.9 billion before leaving theaters (via Box Office Mojo). The race wasn't nearly as tight before then, with Holland's second standalone outing as Peter Parker, Far From Home, reaching $1.13 billion, while the Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield Spider-Man movies failed to cross the $1 billion mark throughout any individual releases in their respective series.

Brand New Day still finds itself in familiar company. The MCU still has two other installments – Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame – in the $2 billion club. Other qualifiers in the category include James Cameron's Avatar and its sequel, Star Wars: Episode 7 – The Force Awakens, and Ne Zha 2.

While Marvel and Brand New Day's accomplishment is no doubt notable, it's anything but a surprise. The film broke records in its opening weekend and only took a few days to earn its first billion dollars. The path to $2 billion was paved early thanks to strong reception from fans and critics, with its big reveals mostly left out of trailers as Cretton and company relied on a more practical approach to Spider-Man, audiences had a lot to show up for.

Where Holland's new movie will finish is anyone's guess, but it's got a long way to go if it wants to climb to the top of the box office leaderboard. However, it is still the second-fastest project to reach $2 billion, with the crown going to Avengers: Endgame.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day swung into theaters a little more than three weeks ago and is expected to remain on the big screen for a while longer. IGN gave it a 7/10 review, saying it "effectively refocuses on the most reliable pillars of the webslinger: battling inner turmoil, swinging around NYC saving the day, and looking cool while doing so."

For more on the MCU, you can check out what the Spider-Man screenwriters had to say about the debate surrounding Jean Grey. You can also see Marvel's big X-Men cast reveal, as well as the latest Avengers: Doomsday trailer.

media:description.$text:
Did Spider-Man Accidentally Create Mutant Inhibitors?

While we’re talking X-Men, there’s a very big plot point that could potentially be used in the upcoming X-Men reboot movie from Brand New Day: Mutant Inhibitors. Spider-Man spends most of the movie wrestling with his surging arachnid DNA, and how to suppress it. Thanks to some coaching by Bruce Banner (Mark Ruffalo), aka the Hulk, he hits on the idea of an inhibitor chip, which he successfully uses on himself – as well as to suppress Jean’s telepathic powers entirely.

However, both Bruce and MJ (Zendaya) warn him that this technology is extremely dangerous, and potentially suppressing something that needs to be expressed. MJ is more concerned about Peter; but Bruce’s warning is about the ramifications of unleashing technology that can suppress any powers in a world already on edge about the idea of super-powered individuals.

While there have been plenty of riffs about this type of technology throughout the decades, it’s impossible to hear this in a movie that brings mutants into the MCU (ignoring the events of Ms. Marvel and The Marvels, as well as Avengers: Doomsday for the moment) without thinking Spider-Man’s tech, which ends up in the hands of Damage Control, could be used on the burgeoning mutant menace.

Normally in the Marvel Comics it takes the form of Inhibitor Collars, placed around a mutant’s neck. Here, it’s a chip, though Damage Control needs to keep it connected to a power source to keep it going. Point being, there’s probably some refinement there before it pops up in an X-Men movie… But yes, very likely Peter Parker is responsible for something that will become a bane to mutant-kind.

items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
D23's Disney Experiences Showcase, also known as Horizons: A Carousel of Progress, was a night filled with exciting updates for Disney Parks around the world and Disney Cruise Line. There were SO many big reveals, including the name and major attractions of Villains Land, new details on the rides and land of the Cars-themed Piston Peak National Park, previews of the Encanto and Indiana Jones experiences at Animal Kingdom, the reimagining of Disneyland's Tomorrowland, and even the return of Figment and Dreamfinder!

Those were only a handful of the announcements from the show, and we've included all of them below to ensure you don't miss a thing! Be sure to let us know which is your favorite and, if you missed it, you can watch the Disney Experiences Showcase on Disney+ right now!

Walt Disney World's Villains Land Is Officially Called Villains Land, And Its Two Major Attractions Have Been Revealed

Walt Disney World's Villains Land is officially called Villains Land, and we were given some exciting updates on what delightful horrors this new space in Magic kingdom will hold when it opens.

Imagineers chose the name because it fits with the classic naming of the other lands at Magic Kingdom (Fantasyland, Tomorrowland, etc.), and the team believes that makes it feel at home while also allowing them to make it more "devious" than the other lands.

What do we have here 🖤Welcome to Villains Land at Magic Kingdom 🏰 pic.twitter.com/xeRaP9xRDa

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

As for the story of the land, it features a brand new, original take on Disney's iconic villains, and it all begins at the wishing well. Once upon a time, a horribly evil wish was made at this wishing well, and it "corrupted the stone and broke open the structure, spreading the well's poisoned magic throughout the forest." This has drawn our villains to this land, who want to claim this power for themselves. These villains help shape the landscape of the land with their "mighty fortresses and gleaming palaces," and it was teased the size and scale of this area is being compared to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge for true immersion.

And this brings us to the first major attraction, a Maleficent Coaster. The legendary villain from Sleeping Beauty who just wanted an invite to a party will be getting her own attraction, and guests will "race through enchanted briar surrounding her frightening mountaintop fortress - if you're feeling brave enough to answer her invitation." While they didn't dive too deep into this, the Imagineers did tease it will include elements never before attempted on similar attractions.

The second major attraction ia a Mirror Realm Dark Ride hosted by the Magic Mirror himself. The mirror resides beneath the palace of Snow White's Evil Queen, and he'll "magically transport" guests to his mystical Mirror Realm to see how things appear on his side. Once there, guests will be "transfixed by countless Disney Villains conjured in ways only the Magic Mirror can do," and a combination of special effects and physical set pieces will bring all this to life.

Walt Disney World's Monsters, Inc.-Themed Monstropolis Gets New Details and a 2027 Opening Window

Alongside the exciting news that the first part of Walt Disney World's Monsters, Inc.-themed Monstropolis will open in 2027, we learned a lot about what this land at Hollywood Studios will feature.

We'll start at the Glob Theater, which will be home to a brand-new show called 'Welcome to Monstropolis." The monsters in this show will help introduce guests to this land, and "highlight how similar monsters and humans really are." Mike and Sulley will be the hosts, and there should be plenty of monster-filled suprises in store.

Perhaps the most exciting update was for Harryhausen's Restaurant, which will be an actual place to eat. Yes, many of us have dreamed of eating at the spot of Mike and Celia's unfortunate date for years, and we'll soon be able to. The menu will be "unlike anything else" offered at Walt Disney World, and the space will, thankfully, include an Audio-Animatronics figure of the iconic octopus-like sushi chef!

Archie's Scare Pig Pizza is next, which will serve guests delicious slices just like PizzeRizzo did when The Muppets resided in this area. For those unfamiliar, Archie is Fear Tech's beloved six-legged mascot from Monsters University.

Speaking of that film/school, Monsters University Alumni Club will be another space to visit in Monstropolis. This space provides a "who's who of all the student clubs, fraternities, and sororities," and is home to the elite "Scarer's Club, honoring the school's legendary scarers from years past."

For a gift for yourself or a loved on, the Scareporium will be the place to grab something to celebrate your journey into this world of monsters.

We’ve got your latest EYE-witness news 👁️ on all things Monstropolis at Hollywood Studios ⭐ #D23 #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/sTDc8rqIc2

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

While we got a quick animated look at how we will rise 40 feet into the air in just four seconds during take-off of Monstropolis' much-anticipated door coaster, we also learned we'll have to wait a bit longer for that one as it won't open right when the rest of the land will.

Two Attractions and Model Revealed for the Cars-Themed Piston Peak National Park at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom

The Cars-themed Piston Peak National Park land coming to Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom is taking shape and we were treated to the reveal of not only its two main attractions, but also a 225-square-foot scale model that lets guests see what the area will look like when it's completed.

We already knew some of what the first attraction would be, but we now know it's called Cars Ridge Run Rally. This attraction aims to be the "wildest racer in the wheelderness" and will task guests with accomplishing the "fastest lap in the west."

The course will take guests up Piston Peak itself, where the cars will need to traverse an icy, snow-covered mountaintop. The ride will then head down that same mountain for a camelback descent before heading through a geyser field. The race will end by circling the Tankfull geyser before rocketing towards the finish line. To make it even more exciting, Lightning McQueen and Tow Mater will be right at the end will covering the race for Racing Sports Network.

The ride vehicles feature brand-new technology created by Imagineers, and the team promises guests will "feel every bump, drop, and rock because this vehicle’s tires and suspension are truly driving over and reacting to them.” In proper Cars fashion, each ride vehicle will also be its own unique car with its own personality.

Miss Fritter's Daredevil Spin-Along is the name of the second attraction, and it features the "Diva of Demolition" herself from Cars 3. Miss Fritter will appear as a "huge school-bus-sized animatronic" who is hosting her "wildest demolition derby yet."

Tomorrowland to Officially Be Reimagined at Disneyland

The second-to-last announcement of the night was the big reveal that Tomorrowland will be reimagined at Disneyland. Disney Experiences Chairman Thomas Mazloum revealed that this transformation will "honor the legacy of the original land while reimagining its future." The team wants to preserve what guests "cherish most" while still being able to introduce new experiences.

This land will feature new attractions, more open spaces, and "new places for Disneyland guests to dream about the future." This plans for Tomorrowland will "restore the spirit of optimism, innovation and possibility that inspired Walt Disney to create 'a vista into a world of wondrous ideas…' in 1955 and have defined this land for decades."

Dreamfinder and Figment Are Returning for a New Journey Into Imagination at EPCOT

A dream can be a dream come true 💭 We are taking a new journey into imagination at EPCOT with Dreamfinder and Figment 🎩💜 #D23 pic.twitter.com/2ujK91B7ea

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

The show's one more thing was the news that Dreamfinder and Figment will be returning for a new Journey Into Imagination at Walt Disney World's EPCOT. Figment is having a moment these days, and the fans in the room were very excited about this one!

Figment has been at EPCOT since 1983 when Journey Into Imagination first opened, and he was paired with Dreamfinder until the "whimsical dream-chaser" was removed in 1998. Now, this pair will be reunited and will hopefully prove that "imagination is something worth holding onto, no matter how old you are."

Disneyland's Avengers Infinity Defense and Stark Flight Lab to Star Actual MCU Stars, Including Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man

The upcoming Avengers Infinity Defense at Avengers Campus at Disneyland's Disney California Adventure will officially star some of the biggest names in the MCU, including Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man, Chris Hemsworth's Thor, Anthony Mackie's Captain America, Jeremy Renner's Hawkeye, and Iman Vellani's Ms. Marvel.

Avengers Infinity Defense is set to open in 2028 and will see guests helping reassemble the Avengers to battle King Thanos. The journey will take us to locations like Asgard, Wakanda, New York City, and more.

Stark Flight Lab will also be bringing some star power, as it will feature Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man, Anthony Mackie's Captain America, and Brie Larson's Captain Marvel. As a reminder, this attraction will set guests in two-person "gyro-kinetic pods" that will roll along a track before getting picked up by a giant robot arm. This will allow guests to feel as though they are flying like an Avenger like Iron Man.

Animal Kingdom's Encanto Attraction Is Called Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto, and It Brings Back the Film's Cast

The Encanto attraction headed to the new Tropical Americas area of Walt Disney World's Animal Kingdom took center stage at D23, and it was revealed that it will be called Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto. In this attraction, guests are invited to celebrate Antonio's new gift of the ability to speak to animals.

To help tell the story, the main voice actors from Encanto will be reprising their roles, including Stephanie Beatriz (Mirabel), Jessica Darrow (Luisa), and Diane Guerrero (Isabella).

The attraction itself will have no height requirement, so guests will be able to take the whole family on this adventure that will head into Casita itself. Guests will enter the Madrigal's magical home while riding an enchanted piece of furniture, and the experience is meant to be "lively and dynamic."

Some of our familia will be joining in on the magia ✨Jess Darrow, Diane Guerrero and Stephanie Beatriz will be voicing their Encanto characters for Antonio's Fiesta de Encanto coming to Animal Kingdom 🌳 #D23 #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/S30YCyPSns

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

The journey will end upstairs in Antonio's room, which has been transformed into a verdant rainforest filled with animals. In fact, the attraction as a whole will feature over 50 animals, and we got a first look at a very adorable capybara and a toucan riding a donkey. To make everything authentic, Imagineering is partnering with Disney's Animals, Science, and Environment Team to ensure the animals are accurate to Colombia.

Harrison Ford to Be the Actual Model for Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent Attraction's Audio-Animatronics Figure at Walt Disney World's Animal Kingdom

We learned a lot about the upcoming Indiana Jones attraction headed to the Tropical Americas area of Walt Disney World's Animal Kingdom, including its name and that Harrison Ford will serve as the actual model of the attraction's Audio-Animatronics figure. Yes, this will be the first time you'll see his actual face on a Disney attraction anywhere in the world.

We have unearthed Indiana Jones news 🤠 For the first time ever, Harrison Ford is the actual model of the Indiana Jones Audio-Animatronics figure, fear of snakes included 🌳 #D23 #AnimalKingdom #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/NULBc78sUe

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

As for the name, it is officially called Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent. This attraction aims to take guests below an ancient temple ruin, "showcasing Maya culture and its profound connection to nature."

Guests will work with Indy, who is exploring this temple that is near a once water-filled underground cave called a denote. Local legends claim this cave may lead to the Maya Underworld, but it issued to be unfortunately guarded by a terrifying serpentine creature known as a Tsukán. The ride kicks off when guests are sucked through a portal to the underworld, and they'll need to escape "perilous dangers, like monstrous bats, larger-than-life scorpions, fire and flame, and, of course, snakes," if they hope to survive.

Tsukán will come to life as a gigantic Audio-Animatronics figure, and you can check out below what it will look like. Oh, and did we mention it is being sculpted by hand to make it even more life-like?

El Carrusel de los Animalitos Will Feature 22 Hand-Carved Animals as Ride Vehicles

Rounding out the Tropical Americas news, we were given a first look at the 22 hand-carved animals that will serve as the ride vehicles for El Carrusel de los Animalitos. While that sounds cool on its own, these carousel vehicles are actually based on beloved Disney and Pixar characters, including Bambi, Simba, Pua, Kevin, and more.

Disneyland's Coco Attraction Takes Place a Year After the Original and We'll Relive Miguel's Memories of the Land of the Dead

Following the big reveals from Coco 2 and the news that Coco will be a new world in Kingdom Hearts 4, we learned a bit more about the much-anticipated Coco attraction that's headed to Disneyland's Disney California Adventure.

The attraction's stoyline takes place a year after the original film and we'll first enter a "casa museo" that's dedicated to Miguel's great-great grandfather, Héctor Rivera. After that, we'll join Miguel and go on a boat ride through his memories of the Land of the Dead. Oh, it will also have no height requirement.

As previously announced, this attraction takes inspiration from those like Pirates of the Caribbean and Haunted Mansion, and it will feature characters brought to life through Audio-Animatronics technology.

The Lion King at Disneyland Paris' Disney Adventure World to Feature Simba's Final Confrontation with Scar

The Lion King is finally getting its first Disney Parks attraction at Disneyland Paris' Disney Adventure World, and it will take us on a journey through the tale of the classic film, including the happy and "not-so-happy times."

Alongside a 120-foot-high Pride Rock that will send us soaring down a new flume system with a 52-foot drop, we'll also be witnessing the final confrontation between Simba and Scar, Simba's Hakuna Matata moment with Timon and Pumbaa, and more.

This attraction will be part of a larger Lion King-themed area of Disney Adventure World, and it aims to transport guests into the world of the 1994 classic.

POV: You’re getting a front row of The Lion King construction at Disney Adventure World at Disneyland Paris 🦁 #D23 pic.twitter.com/thAX4hMnqn

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Disney Believe's Stern, Bow, and Grand Hall Characters Revealed, New Ship Class Teased

The Disney Believe is getting ready to set sail in 2027, but D23 helped share some exciting details on Disney Cruise Line's fourth Wish-class ship.

First up, we have the grand hall, where Moana, Pua, and Heihei will stand tall in bronze. The whole hall will take influences from the film's South Pacific setting, and Moana will help infuse the space with the "optimistic spirit of exploration."

Going outside, we learned that Woody and Buzz would be serving as the Believe's stern characters. In an adorable touch, the Toy Story duo are drawing the ships name with crayons.

A hand-painted filigree of Tinker Bell will the star of the Believe's bow decoration, which will also include silhouettes of Peter, Wendy, Captain Hook, and more.

Lastly, Disney Cruise Line teased its newest class of ships that will sit between the newer Wish-class ships and the classic ones. The first of these ships won't sail until 2029, but we now have a better idea as to how they look!

A sneak peek of the newest class of Disney Cruise Line ships sailing into your feed 🚢 #D23 pic.twitter.com/dS3FP7sPVD

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Carousel of Progress Casts Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-Winning Actor Bryan Cranston

Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-winning actor Bryan Cranston will voice Mom and Dad in Carousel of Progress at Magic Kingdom 🏰 #D23 #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/1MZvwhiUxZ

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Alongside a glimpse of the new scenes set in the 1980s, it was revealed that Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-winning actor Bryan Cranston will be joining the cast as the new version of the attraction's Mom and Dad, respectively.

This is all part of Carousel of Progress' big new update that will send it forward by decades. In late spring 2027, the story will span from the 1960s to the far, far future, and Walt Disney, as an Audio-Animatronics figure, will welcome guests in an all-new introductory scene.

EPCOT's Spaceship Earth Will Be Reimagined With a Focus on 'Human Connection'

Everyone's favorite geodesic sphere at EPCOT is getting reimagined for the first time in almost 20 years. While the current iteration focuses on the story of human communication, this new take will "focus on a broader theme that is still classically EPCOT - human connection."

While the current Spaceship Earth takes guests from prehistoric times to the 21st century, the new one bring the attraction to the "internet age and beyond."

The Yeti Audio-Animatronic Is Coming Back to Life at Animal Kingdom's Expedition Everest

At the showcase, Disney Experiences Chairman Thomas Mazloum revealed that the team is "bringing the Yeti back to life inside Expedition Everest at Disney's Animal Kingdom!" This is a big deal for Disney fans as the original Yeti Audio-Animatronics figure's framing split just a few months after the attraction opened back in 2006.

This has caused the figure to live in its "B-Mode," where it uses a strobe light effect to make it appear as though it was moving. This has lovingly earned the figure the moniker of "Disco Yeti," and it looks like that version will soon be put to rest atop the treacherous mountain.

The Imagineering Season 2 Is Headed to Disney+ in Early 2028

Back for more ✨ The Imagineering Story season 2 debuts on @DisneyPlus in 2028 🦾 #D23 pic.twitter.com/W9lMNeT1E9

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Leslie Iwerks' The Imagineering Story is one of the most beloved documentaries on Disney+, and it was just revealed that we'd be getting a second season in early 2028. The first season focused on the origins of the Imagineers, and these new episodes will follow them as they "help shape one of the most ambitious periods in Disney Experiences history."

Iwerks is also getting ready to release Disney Worldbuilders on August 20 on Disney+, and you can check out our interview with her and thoughts on her Disneyland Handcrafted documentary here.

The Avengers and Spider-Man Will Soon Also Call Hong Kong Disneyland and Shanghai Disney Resort Home

Internationally, Avengers Research Testing Labs is under construction at Hong Kong Disneyland Resort. When finished, guests will interact with Stark Industries and other heroes like Peter Parker / Spider-Man. Don't expect everything to go smooth however, as the threat of villains is always present.

Using "120+ feet of storytelling tech," the story will unfold across such locations as Wakanda, Asgard, and more, and there will be plenty of heroes joining you along the way.

For a less thrilling but still awesome adventure, guests will then be able to head over to the Quinjet landing platform to encounter their favorite MCU characters.

At Shanghai Disney Resort, work continues on the fest-ever Spider-Man-theme land and thrill attraction. This section is home to the new Shanghai division of the Worldwide Engineering Brigade (W.E.B. for short!), and it will be where Peter Parker and his friends have created some Spider-Bots to not only help them with experiments, but also build a brand-new coaster.

What's a truly special touch, local artists are being tapped to create more than 20 murals throughout this new land, adding a unique touch to an already intriguing and exciting space. As for how along the team is? The final piece of the attraction's track has officially been installed!

Space Mountain Getting Big Upgrades at Tokyo Disneyland and Disneyland Paris

Tokyo Disneyland and Disneyland Paris' Space Mountains are getting some major upgrades, and we learned a bit more about these projects at D23.

In Tokyo Disneyland, guests will soon be able to ride Space Mountain: Earthrise, which will let guests launch "into the cosmos and experience the wonder of Earth from a perspective unlike anything seen before in a Disney attraction." This will be just one part of the park's reimagined Tomorrowland.

In Disneyland Paris, Space Mountain: De la Terre à la Lune will be a reimagined experience that draws inspiration from the Jules Verne story that actually helped shape the original attraction. This updated ride will feature the attraction's original musical score and a "refreshed experience." The current version of the park's Space Mountain will closes at the end of 2027 to make way for this new era.

Disneyland Resort to Bring Back Classic Entertainment (Two Nighttime Spectaculars and One Daytime Parade!)

For those looking to enter a time long gone, Disneyland is bringing back some beloved classic entertainment, including two nighttime spectaculars and one daytime parade.

The first nighttime spectacular is 'Remember... Dreams Come True,' which will debut in February 2027 and first appeared during Disneyland's 50th anniversary. Julie Andrews provided the vocal introduction of this show, and it aims to once again illustrate the "power of wishes and dreams in favorite Disney stories." Guests will also be able to look forward to new projections on Sleeping Beauty Castle, Rivers of America, the facade of it's a small world, and Main Street, U.S.A.

The second classic nighttime spectacular returning is the original 'World of Color' at Disney California Adventure, which will once again feature a journey through such beloved animated classics like The Little Mermaid, The Lion King, Finding Nemo, and Toy Story. It also features a special arrangement of the theme song from Walt Disney's Wonderful World of Color TV show from the 1960s.

Lastly, the 'Magic Happens' daytime parade will come roaring back in summer 2027 to Disneyland. This parade will be led by Mickey Mouse and his friends, and also stars Cinderella, The Sword in the Stone, Coco, and surprises like pumpkins becoming carriages and swords being "plucked from a stone."

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

The journey will end upstairs in Antonio's room, which has been transformed into a verdant rainforest filled with animals. In fact, the attraction as a whole will feature over 50 animals, and we got a first look at a very adorable capybara and a toucan riding a donkey. To make everything authentic, Imagineering is partnering with Disney's Animals, Science, and Environment Team to ensure the animals are accurate to Colombia.

Harrison Ford to Be the Actual Model for Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent Attraction's Audio-Animatronics Figure at Walt Disney World's Animal Kingdom

We learned a lot about the upcoming Indiana Jones attraction headed to the Tropical Americas area of Walt Disney World's Animal Kingdom, including its name and that Harrison Ford will serve as the actual model of the attraction's Audio-Animatronics figure. Yes, this will be the first time you'll see his actual face on a Disney attraction anywhere in the world.

We have unearthed Indiana Jones news 🤠 For the first time ever, Harrison Ford is the actual model of the Indiana Jones Audio-Animatronics figure, fear of snakes included 🌳 #D23 #AnimalKingdom #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/NULBc78sUe

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

As for the name, it is officially called Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent. This attraction aims to take guests below an ancient temple ruin, "showcasing Maya culture and its profound connection to nature."

Guests will work with Indy, who is exploring this temple that is near a once water-filled underground cave called a denote. Local legends claim this cave may lead to the Maya Underworld, but it issued to be unfortunately guarded by a terrifying serpentine creature known as a Tsukán. The ride kicks off when guests are sucked through a portal to the underworld, and they'll need to escape "perilous dangers, like monstrous bats, larger-than-life scorpions, fire and flame, and, of course, snakes," if they hope to survive.

Tsukán will come to life as a gigantic Audio-Animatronics figure, and you can check out below what it will look like. Oh, and did we mention it is being sculpted by hand to make it even more life-like?

El Carrusel de los Animalitos Will Feature 22 Hand-Carved Animals as Ride Vehicles

Rounding out the Tropical Americas news, we were given a first look at the 22 hand-carved animals that will serve as the ride vehicles for El Carrusel de los Animalitos. While that sounds cool on its own, these carousel vehicles are actually based on beloved Disney and Pixar characters, including Bambi, Simba, Pua, Kevin, and more.

Disneyland's Coco Attraction Takes Place a Year After the Original and We'll Relive Miguel's Memories of the Land of the Dead

Following the big reveals from Coco 2 and the news that Coco will be a new world in Kingdom Hearts 4, we learned a bit more about the much-anticipated Coco attraction that's headed to Disneyland's Disney California Adventure.

The attraction's stoyline takes place a year after the original film and we'll first enter a "casa museo" that's dedicated to Miguel's great-great grandfather, Héctor Rivera. After that, we'll join Miguel and go on a boat ride through his memories of the Land of the Dead. Oh, it will also have no height requirement.

As previously announced, this attraction takes inspiration from those like Pirates of the Caribbean and Haunted Mansion, and it will feature characters brought to life through Audio-Animatronics technology.

The Lion King at Disneyland Paris' Disney Adventure World to Feature Simba's Final Confrontation with Scar

The Lion King is finally getting its first Disney Parks attraction at Disneyland Paris' Disney Adventure World, and it will take us on a journey through the tale of the classic film, including the happy and "not-so-happy times."

Alongside a 120-foot-high Pride Rock that will send us soaring down a new flume system with a 52-foot drop, we'll also be witnessing the final confrontation between Simba and Scar, Simba's Hakuna Matata moment with Timon and Pumbaa, and more.

This attraction will be part of a larger Lion King-themed area of Disney Adventure World, and it aims to transport guests into the world of the 1994 classic.

POV: You’re getting a front row of The Lion King construction at Disney Adventure World at Disneyland Paris 🦁 #D23 pic.twitter.com/thAX4hMnqn

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Disney Believe's Stern, Bow, and Grand Hall Characters Revealed, New Ship Class Teased

The Disney Believe is getting ready to set sail in 2027, but D23 helped share some exciting details on Disney Cruise Line's fourth Wish-class ship.

First up, we have the grand hall, where Moana, Pua, and Heihei will stand tall in bronze. The whole hall will take influences from the film's South Pacific setting, and Moana will help infuse the space with the "optimistic spirit of exploration."

Going outside, we learned that Woody and Buzz would be serving as the Believe's stern characters. In an adorable touch, the Toy Story duo are drawing the ships name with crayons.

A hand-painted filigree of Tinker Bell will the star of the Believe's bow decoration, which will also include silhouettes of Peter, Wendy, Captain Hook, and more.

Lastly, Disney Cruise Line teased its newest class of ships that will sit between the newer Wish-class ships and the classic ones. The first of these ships won't sail until 2029, but we now have a better idea as to how they look!

A sneak peek of the newest class of Disney Cruise Line ships sailing into your feed 🚢 #D23 pic.twitter.com/dS3FP7sPVD

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Carousel of Progress Casts Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-Winning Actor Bryan Cranston

Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-winning actor Bryan Cranston will voice Mom and Dad in Carousel of Progress at Magic Kingdom 🏰 #D23 #WaltDisneyWorld pic.twitter.com/1MZvwhiUxZ

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Alongside a glimpse of the new scenes set in the 1980s, it was revealed that Disney Legend Jamie Lee Curtis and Emmy-winning actor Bryan Cranston will be joining the cast as the new version of the attraction's Mom and Dad, respectively.

This is all part of Carousel of Progress' big new update that will send it forward by decades. In late spring 2027, the story will span from the 1960s to the far, far future, and Walt Disney, as an Audio-Animatronics figure, will welcome guests in an all-new introductory scene.

EPCOT's Spaceship Earth Will Be Reimagined With a Focus on 'Human Connection'

Everyone's favorite geodesic sphere at EPCOT is getting reimagined for the first time in almost 20 years. While the current iteration focuses on the story of human communication, this new take will "focus on a broader theme that is still classically EPCOT - human connection."

While the current Spaceship Earth takes guests from prehistoric times to the 21st century, the new one bring the attraction to the "internet age and beyond."

The Yeti Audio-Animatronic Is Coming Back to Life at Animal Kingdom's Expedition Everest

At the showcase, Disney Experiences Chairman Thomas Mazloum revealed that the team is "bringing the Yeti back to life inside Expedition Everest at Disney's Animal Kingdom!" This is a big deal for Disney fans as the original Yeti Audio-Animatronics figure's framing split just a few months after the attraction opened back in 2006.

This has caused the figure to live in its "B-Mode," where it uses a strobe light effect to make it appear as though it was moving. This has lovingly earned the figure the moniker of "Disco Yeti," and it looks like that version will soon be put to rest atop the treacherous mountain.

The Imagineering Season 2 Is Headed to Disney+ in Early 2028

Back for more ✨ The Imagineering Story season 2 debuts on @DisneyPlus in 2028 🦾 #D23 pic.twitter.com/W9lMNeT1E9

— Disney Parks (@DisneyParks) August 16, 2026

Leslie Iwerks' The Imagineering Story is one of the most beloved documentaries on Disney+, and it was just revealed that we'd be getting a second season in early 2028. The first season focused on the origins of the Imagineers, and these new episodes will follow them as they "help shape one of the most ambitious periods in Disney Experiences history."

Iwerks is also getting ready to release Disney Worldbuilders on August 20 on Disney+, and you can check out our interview with her and thoughts on her Disneyland Handcrafted documentary here.

The Avengers and Spider-Man Will Soon Also Call Hong Kong Disneyland and Shanghai Disney Resort Home

Internationally, Avengers Research Testing Labs is under construction at Hong Kong Disneyland Resort. When finished, guests will interact with Stark Industries and other heroes like Peter Parker / Spider-Man. Don't expect everything to go smooth however, as the threat of villains is always present.

Using "120+ feet of storytelling tech," the story will unfold across such locations as Wakanda, Asgard, and more, and there will be plenty of heroes joining you along the way.

For a less thrilling but still awesome adventure, guests will then be able to head over to the Quinjet landing platform to encounter their favorite MCU characters.

At Shanghai Disney Resort, work continues on the fest-ever Spider-Man-theme land and thrill attraction. This section is home to the new Shanghai division of the Worldwide Engineering Brigade (W.E.B. for short!), and it will be where Peter Parker and his friends have created some Spider-Bots to not only help them with experiments, but also build a brand-new coaster.

What's a truly special touch, local artists are being tapped to create more than 20 murals throughout this new land, adding a unique touch to an already intriguing and exciting space. As for how along the team is? The final piece of the attraction's track has officially been installed!

Space Mountain Getting Big Upgrades at Tokyo Disneyland and Disneyland Paris

Tokyo Disneyland and Disneyland Paris' Space Mountains are getting some major upgrades, and we learned a bit more about these projects at D23.

In Tokyo Disneyland, guests will soon be able to ride Space Mountain: Earthrise, which will let guests launch "into the cosmos and experience the wonder of Earth from a perspective unlike anything seen before in a Disney attraction." This will be just one part of the park's reimagined Tomorrowland.

In Disneyland Paris, Space Mountain: De la Terre à la Lune will be a reimagined experience that draws inspiration from the Jules Verne story that actually helped shape the original attraction. This updated ride will feature the attraction's original musical score and a "refreshed experience." The current version of the park's Space Mountain will closes at the end of 2027 to make way for this new era.

Disneyland Resort to Bring Back Classic Entertainment (Two Nighttime Spectaculars and One Daytime Parade!)

For those looking to enter a time long gone, Disneyland is bringing back some beloved classic entertainment, including two nighttime spectaculars and one daytime parade.

The first nighttime spectacular is 'Remember... Dreams Come True,' which will debut in February 2027 and first appeared during Disneyland's 50th anniversary. Julie Andrews provided the vocal introduction of this show, and it aims to once again illustrate the "power of wishes and dreams in favorite Disney stories." Guests will also be able to look forward to new projections on Sleeping Beauty Castle, Rivers of America, the facade of it's a small world, and Main Street, U.S.A.

The second classic nighttime spectacular returning is the original 'World of Color' at Disney California Adventure, which will once again feature a journey through such beloved animated classics like The Little Mermaid, The Lion King, Finding Nemo, and Toy Story. It also features a special arrangement of the theme song from Walt Disney's Wonderful World of Color TV show from the 1960s.

Lastly, the 'Magic Happens' daytime parade will come roaring back in summer 2027 to Disneyland. This parade will be led by Mickey Mouse and his friends, and also stars Cinderella, The Sword in the Stone, Coco, and surprises like pumpkins becoming carriages and swords being "plucked from a stone."

items.title: 'I Want to Set the Record Straight: That Is Not Happening' — Kingdom Hearts 4 Devs Say KH4 '100%' Will Not Be Delayed Past Late 2027 Launch | D23 2026
items.description: Kingdom Hearts 4 co-director Tai Yasue and series creator Tetsuya Nomura have assured fans that it is a "100% thing" the game will not be delayed past its late 2027 launch window.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Kingdom Hearts 4 co-director Tai Yasue and series creator Tetsuya Nomura have assured fans that it is a "100% thing" the game will not be delayed past its late 2027 launch window.

While the team behind the new Kingdom Hearts game stopped short of sharing a final release date during its big D23 2026 presence, they feel pretty confident the current schedule will stick. Yasue, Nomura, and director of product development at Disney and Pixar games Nana Gadd doubled down on Square Enix's Kingdom Hearts 4 launch plans during a panel at this year's show.

"One last thing I wanted to share: We announced the game is going to be coming in late 2027," Nomura said. "I saw online that some people were saying the release date might still get pushed back. I want to set the record straight: That is not happening. I do hope that people do look forward to the game coming in 2027. A lot of the marketing for the game has only just started, and so I do hope that people also look forward to hearing more news as well."

"There's many things underway, many plans we have underway," he continued. "Now that we are approaching the 25th anniversary, we're thinking about what the 30th anniversary [looks like]."

"I can confidently say and promise that it will launch in 2027," Yasue said. "Schedule-wise, the development is very smooth. It's not like an 80%, 90% – it's a 100% thing. We'll be there in 2027 for sure."

The more skeptical fans believe they have some justification for their delay fears. Mainline entries in the series have suffered infamously long breaks between entries, with the break between Kingdom Hearts 2 and 3 being 13 years. We're now going on eight years since the last game's launch in 2019, but it sounds like the developers at Square Enix are confident the wait won't be too much longer.

Another reason fans are worried about a delay relates to the recent conversation surrounding physical game discs. Sony announced in July that it will no longer support physical releases for new PlayStation games that launch after January 2028. Should Kingdom Hearts 4 be delayed past that date, it would make it the first mainline entry in the series without a physical release, at least on PlayStation 5. For now, however, Square Enix has yet to confirm any other details surrounding its launch.

Kingdom Hearts 4 was formally announced in 2022 and will launch for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox Series X | S in late 2027. While we wait to see what other Disney worlds and, hopefully, Final Fantasy characters the team have planned for the fourth games, you can read about the the extended gameplay trailer shown during the panel. You can also catch up on everything announced during the D23 panel right here.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts 4 Gets Extended Gameplay Trailer Featuring Playable Mickey, Donald, and Goofy | D23 2026
items.description: Disney and Square Enix showed up for the Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel at D23 2026 to show off an extended gameplay trailer for Kingdom Hearts 4 that features a first look at a playable King Mickey, Donald, and Goofy.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Disney and Square Enix showed up for the Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel at D23 2026 to show off an extended gameplay trailer for Kingdom Hearts 4 that features a first look at a playable King Mickey, Donald, and Goofy.

No one expected Sora to show up in the world of Pixar's Coco, Keyblade in hand, when the legendary crossover franchise made a surprise appearance during yesterday's Disney Entertainment Showcase. That only made Mickey, Donald, and Goofy showing up as playable characters in today's new four-minute trailer even more of a shock.

Gameplay for Goofy and Donald seems to mostly fall in line with what we've come to expect from Sora. Outside of one segment that saw the two Disney icons sledding through the Underworld, they can be seen using abilities and teaming up to fight off Heartless enemies.

King Mickey, meanwhile, has received some special attention. The first clip shows him walking around from a third-person point of view before switching to origami-like visuals featuring 2D and 3D gameplay. It looks heavily inspired by Nintendo's Paper Mario, though how long all of these sections will be remains to be seen.

Another surprise saved for today's lengthier look at the game is Riku, who shows up in the video's final moments. He doesn't stick around for too long before the video comes to an end, but it looks like he'll be teaming up with Sora for at least part of Kingdom Hearts 4's events.

Elsewhere during the panel, series creator Tetsuya Nomura refuted claims that the game would eventually be delayed outside of its 2027 launch window. It's been a big weekend for Kingdom Hearts fans, as Disney and Square Enix have also confirmed plans to release an anime series based on the franchise at some point in the future.

Kingdom Hearts 4 is still on track to launch in its late 2027 release window for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X | S. While we wait for updates, be sure to check out everything announced from the panel here.

items.title: Tetsuya Nomura Teases Involvement in Kingdom Hearts Anime Series, Tells Fans to Let Their 'Imagination Run Wild' | D23 2026
items.description: Kingdom Hearts creator Tetsuya Nomura has one message for fans when it comes to its mysterious new Disney+ anime series: "Please let your imagination run wild."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Kingdom Hearts creator Tetsuya Nomura has one message for fans when it comes to its mysterious new Disney+ anime series: "Please let your imagination run wild."

The Square Enix and Final Fantasy veteran shared a message with excited fans on X/Twitter after the crossover series made a surprise appearance at last night's D23 2026 Disney Entertainment Showcase. Its presence came not only with a first look at how the next mainline installment in the franchise will incorporate the world of Pixar's Coco but also a teaser for a new Kingdom Hearts series coming to Disney+.

Unfortunately, the big reveal shared little about how the anime project will actually fit into Kingdom Hearts' infamously tangled timeline. For now, all fans have to go off of are a few words from Disney Kids & Family president Ayo Davis and some ethereal art featuring what appears to be a new Keyblade-wielding character. Where Nomura could have intervened to clear the air, he instead chose to encourage speculation from those who are no doubt already spinning theories.

"Production of a Kingdom Hearts animated series has been confirmed," Nomura's message said (via Google Translate). "I imagine this sudden announcement came as a surprise. You are likely wondering what the series will be about. While I cannot share specific details just yet, I have been holding close consultations with the scenario team—and the art team, when necessary—and we have even created new character designs specifically for this project.

"I cannot say anything more at this moment, but the single piece of key art released serves as a hint. Please let your imagination run wild as you await further updates."

Filling long waits with theories is something Kingdom Hearts fans are especially skilled at. Outside of the odd spinoff project, the franchise has seen long gaps between releases. Kingdom Hearts 3, for example, launched a brutal 13 years after Kingdom Hearts 2. By the time Kingdom Hearts 4 reaches its recently announced 2027 release window, it will have been around eight years since the last numbered entry – and that's if there are no delays.

The Kingdom Hearts anime series, however, doesn't actually have a release date – or even a window – for fans to mark on their calendars. The art only tells viewers that it's "coming soon" to Disney+.

"Kingdom Hearts has captivated gamers everywhere with its unique blend of adventure and imagination," Davis said following the reveal. "There’s something really exciting about taking a world fans have spent years exploring through the games and bringing it to life in a completely new way. And with a creative team that is working closely with the legendary Tetsuya Nomura, our new series will be unmistakably Kingdom Hearts, while giving fans a whole new way to experience the world they love."

It's unclear when we'll learn more about the show, but there is a chance we get some details later today. Disney will soon host its Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel as part of this year's D23. We'll be keeping track of all of the biggest updates here. For more, you can see how Kingdom Hearts 4 reappeared for a Nintendo Direct earlier this year. You can also see why Disney Animation isn't writing off a movie based on the series just yet.

items.title: D23 Deep Dive Into Kingdom Hearts Panel: Everything Announced
items.description: D23, Disney's biggest fan convention, continues with a special panel all about Kingdom Hearts. IGN is on the ground bringing you the biggest news, reveals, and updates from the presentation as it kicks off today, August 15.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
D23, Disney's biggest fan convention, continues with a special panel all about Kingdom Hearts. IGN is on the ground bringing you the biggest news, reveals, and updates from the presentation as it kicks off today, August 15.

Titled ‘DEEP DIVE into KINGDOM HEARTS,’ this panel will stream live starting 4:30 PM PT / 7:30 PM ET / August 16 at 12:30 AM UK Time. You can watch it on IGN's own YouTube channel, which we will embed in this article for your convenience once the show gets started.

Disney said the panel will give fans a "behind-the-scenes look at the making of the games,” with insights from the "creative minds, character voices, and more behind the magic."

Guests on the panel include Nana Gadd, director of games at the Walt Disney Company's Japan branch, Tai Yasue from Square Enix, Haley Joel Osment, the voice of Sora, David Gallagher, the voice of Riku, and Renée Johnson, who is behind several Disney character voices.

This event follows gameplay footage shown at D23's Friday night showcase at the Honda Center the day prior, where fans got to see Sora battling the Heartless in Coco's Land of the Dead. A Kingdom Hearts animated series was also announced, which will stream on Disney+ on an as-yet unreleased date.

Follow along starting at 4:30 PM PT / 7:30 PM ET for all of the latest updates from what's shaping up to be one of the most highly-anticipated looks at Kingdom Hearts 4 and what's next for the series.

And that's a wrap!

Thanks for keeping it locked to IGN for our live report of D23's Deep Dive into Kingdom Hearts panel. And remember — let your heart be your guiding key!

Haley Joel Osment and David Gallagher Take the Stage

Haley Joel Osment, David Gallagher, and Renée Johnson came up on stage, where they discussed their experiences working on Kingdom Hearts over the years.

Johnson showed off an adorable scrapbook of images taken from production during Kingdom Hearts 1, which one of her colleague's wives made all those years ago. It was seriously cute and a major throwback for both the actors and the KH fanbase.

Osment joked about how he has to change his voice to sound more like his younger self, saying it feels like his eyes are about to "pop out" of his head when he's recording Sora these days. Gallagher remarked that his 17-year-old self was shocked at playing a 'bad guy' in Riku, saying he was used to being a 'golden boy' up until that point.

Miyu Irino, the Japanese voice actor for Sora, also appeared in a short video to send fans a message thanking them for their support over the years.

items.title: Dave Filoni Confirms Disney Isn't Making Scrapped Star Wars Movie The Hunt for Ben Solo 'Right Now' | D23 2026
items.description: Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has confirmed that, despite the push from fans, Disney still isn't working on its scrapped Star Wars movie The Hunt for Ben Solo.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has confirmed that, despite the push from fans, Disney still isn't working on its scrapped Star Wars movie The Hunt for Ben Solo.

Variety pressed The Clone Wars orchestrator about the shelved Steven Soderbergh project after last night's Disney Entertainment Showcase at D23 2026. Considering fans have been pushing Disney and Lucasfilm to bring Adam Driver's Kylo Ren back for The Hunt for Ben Solo for months, it shouldn't be a surprise to hear Filoni has been expecting to be asked about the project for some time.

"You know, someone was going to ask me that in this line," he said with a smile. "I'm surprised it took this long, so that's really cool."

Dave Filoni confirms that Lucasfilm is not making “The Hunt for Ben Solo” right now. #D23 pic.twitter.com/pH414RuZtc

— Variety (@Variety) August 15, 2026

Filoni, gesturing with a reference to the Jedi's hand-waving mind tricks, then said, "We're not making that picture right now. That's all I can say."

He had a similar response for Deadline: "It’s not here, you won’t find it here. The force is not with us in that regard; I love the love you feel for it."

Fans perked up with the hope for more sequel trilogy Star Wars when Driver spilled the beans about a shelved project last October. He said the project was in development with the title The Hunt for Ben Solo and had been worked on by he and Soderbergh for two years before Disney pulled the plug. At the time, the Traffic director said, "I really enjoyed making the movie in my head. I’m just sorry the fans won’t get to see it."

Even former Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said The Hunt for Ben Solo's script was "great," but that didn't stop Disney from setting the film aside. Considering Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker left Kylo Ren's story on a bit of a sour note, intensity from fans has really only ramped up the last few months. While some flew a "Save The Hunt for Ben Solo" banner over Walt Disney Studios, others waited for the premiere of this year's The Mandalorian and Grogu to voice their dissatisfaction.

Although Soderbergh went on to call the move to scrap the movie "insane," adding that Disney got "two and a half years of free work" from him, Driver, and screenwriter Rebecca Blunt, it doesn't sound like he's been hopeful that the project could rematerialize. When asked in April if there was a possibility of The Hunt for Ben Solo being revived, he said, "nope."

"If it was gonna happen, it would have happened," Soderbergh told The Playlist. "It's that simple."

With Filoni now in charge of Lucasfilm, it sounds like that possibility still isn't high, at least not yet. His tongue-in-cheek answer does at least suggest the Star Wars minds at Disney are more than aware that it's something fans want to see, though.

In the meantime, Star Wars is chugging ahead. Following The Mandalorian and Grogu's premiere in May, the franchise is set to continue on Disney+ with Ahsoka Season 2 thanks to its newly revealed January 2027 release date. D23 also gave IGN a sneak peek at the first trailer for 2027's Star Wars: Starfighter. You can catch up on all of the event's biggest announcements right here.

items.title: X-Men Director Teases Comic Book Inspirations and 'Something New' for the MCU After Marvel's Big Cast Reveal | D23 2026
items.description: X-Men director Jake Schreier has teased some of the comic book inspirations for his new MCU reboot, saying that he's already talked to Marvel Studios about finding the "things that haven't recently been done well" in the movies.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
X-Men director Jake Schreier has teased some of the comic book inspirations for his new MCU reboot, saying that he's already talked to Marvel Studios about finding the "things that haven't recently been done well" in the movies.

The filmmaker leading the charge on what seems to be the first post-Avengers: Secret Wars movie spoke about some of the corners of the mutant universe he and MCU boss Kevin Feige have already started digging through during an interview with Good Morning America. The conversation followed the film's explosive D23 2026 X-Men cast reveal, which included announcements for characters like Rogue, Storm, Professor X, and Mister Sinister.

With its May 2028 release still almost two years away, Schreier, who previously helmed Marvel's Thunderbolts*, stopped short of revealing too much about the movie's plot. Instead, his comments suggested fans may want to brush up on the work of comic book authors Chris Claremont and Jonathan Hickman.

"One of the great things about the comics is there is such a rich and broad history," he said. "That was one of the first things that Kevin and I talked about when I came in; they made many great movies in this world, and they've made so many great things. Let's find the things that haven't recently been done well. All these other corners of the universe…"

"Digging back into those comics like 20 years, the whole Chris Claremont run, the newer Jonathan Hickman stuff. There are so many stories that are still untold, to honor and to reach into, and then to meet this cast and try to do something new, I think you always want to see something that reveres where it came from and then is still taking a new spin on where we want to go."

As teased by Feige, Schreier's MCU X-Men team is still coming together, but they've got after last night, it's clear there's already a pretty solid foundation in place. The D23 reveal saw Inde Navarrette confirmed as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, and Adam Driver as Mister Sinister. Joining them on stage were a few previously announced parts, including Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, and Sadie Sink as Jean Grey.

Earlier in the same interview, Connor teased his connection to the X-Men. He also teased a new direction for the mutant superhero group for the 2028 film.

"I grew up with the original movies in a lot of ways, and it's really cool because it also feels like we are doing a really different version, a different take, which is really exciting."

As of last night, X-Men is confirmed to premiere May 5, 2028. Ghost Rider is also due out that year but does not have a date, with Black Panther 3 locked in to arrive December 15, 2028.

Up next on the MCU calendar is VisionQuest in October and Avengers: Doomsday in December, with both receiving new trailers at D23, too. For more, you can read all about the biggest reveals from the show.

items.title: Frozen 3 Footage Teases New Villain, and It Looks Like Olaf is Getting a Love Interest
items.description: Disney has shown off a first look at Frozen 3 at its fan event, D23.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney has shown off a first look at Frozen 3 at its fan event, D23.

The section on the company's hugely-anticipated Frozen threequel capped off the evening's festivities, beginning with a rather ominous tune sung by Idina Menzel and Kristen Bell. Next up was a romantic number for Olaf the snowman sung by Josh Gad, before a clip from what looked to be early in the new film that revealed its villain.

Frozen 3 will pick up the action as Anna and Kristoff finally get married, an event which brings the whole gang, including Elsa, Olaf and Sven the reindeer, to get back together. But on the evening of the ceremony, a mysterious curtain of Northern Lights descends upon Arendelle's fjord, heralding the arrival of a new threat.

Lyrics sung by Menzel and Bell describe this moment: "she sends an invitation from the Northern Lights so shining" which is later referred to as a "cursed frozen heart."

"Doesn't it feel like the world of Frozen is a bit different?" Bell said afterwards, before Menzel agreed that their characters were "going on their biggest journey yet."

Of course, the series' humor will not be lost despite a seemingly darker turn. Taking to the stage, Gad sang a funky romantic tune suggesting Olaf will fall in love — with a character named Samantha, a perfect callback to Frozen 2.

After all of that wrapped up, it was time for that Frozen 3 footage, which began with a jagged snowflake fluttering down across Arendelle, until it's stopped by Elsa — frozen into an ice block. Elsa is curious, and as the rest of the gang turn up ("they were doing mouth to mouth stuff!" shouts Olaf of the newly-weds), a glittering frozen walkway appears, stretching into the Northern Lights.

There's some lighter stuff here, as Anna chides Kristoff for not carrying her wedding dress train, and Olaf celebrates catching the bouquet, but quickly Elsa meets a mysterious and threatening figure.

"Look what the Northern Lights dragged in," the figure exclaims, her face left unseen. Dressed in a dark cloak and surrounded by more jagged snowflakes, the character certainly has a malevolent presence. "The famous sisters of Arendelle! We finally meet," the voice says... and that's the end of the trailer.

Frozen 3 is set to launch in theaters on November 24, 2027, eight years on from 2019's Frozen 2, with all of the franchise's core cast returning. Earlier this year, Kristen Bell played down a report that claimed she was set to pocket $60 million for voicing Anna in Frozen 3 and the already-confirmed Frozen 4 — while acknowledging she was still paid "very well" overall for the blockbuster Disney franchise.

From Star Wars to Marvel, Tangled to Kingdom Hearts, catch up on everything announced at D23 2026 right here.

Image credit: Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney

items.title: Disney Animation Studios Boss Jared Bush Isn't Ruling Out a Possible Kingdom Hearts Movie
items.description: Jared Bush, chief creative officer of Walt Disney Animation Studios, spoke about the possibility of a Kingdom Hearts feature film, and he didn’t rule out the idea.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Jared Bush, chief creative officer of Walt Disney Animation Studios, spoke about the possibility of a Kingdom Hearts feature film, and he didn’t rule out the idea.

Kingdom Hearts fans are on top of the world after footage of the fourth game was shown off at D23. Sora and the gang are back to fight the heartless, which are wreaking havoc in the Land of the Dead. Coco’s universe is an explorable world in Kingdom Hearts IV, and Sora even gets a keyblade themed after Héctor's Guitar, along with some calavera facepaint to match.

A Kingdom Hearts animated series was also announced at the event, coming to Disney+ on an as-yet undetermined date. With these two big reveals in mind, IGN’s Jeffrey Vega quizzed Walt Disney Animation Studios’ Jared Bush if there’s anything more planned for the Kingdom Hearts world on Disney’s side of things… specifically, a feature-length animated film.

“Are we ever gonna get a Kingdom Hearts movie?” Vega asked, going on to joke that Bush basically has the power to “greenlight” the project.

“Technically, you’re not wrong,” Bush answered. “I’d say, I’m always excited to hear what people are passionate about. And I’d say that we have a very bright future of new projects coming out — different ways of putting material out into the world. So I would just say, nothing is impossible.”

Bush’s response was, as expected, quite reserved, but his open-ended answer leaves no end of possibilities to the imagination. Given all the good news fans just got about the franchise, specifically the animated show, the idea of a full-length CGI movie following Sora’s adventures doesn’t seem so impossible now... especially since Disney recently bragged that Kingdom Hearts is one of its "billion-dollar franchises."

Kingdom Hearts IV is scheduled for release in late 2027. Combat footage from Coco’s section of the game seen at D23 shows Sora using the keyblade as a kind of skateboard as he follows a flying heartless, to which he’s tethered by a glowing chain. Graphically, the game looks absolutely stunning, with the endless city of the dead giving an impressive depth to the environment.

This most recent trailer also showed off Mickey, Goofy, and our iconic king of the underworld, Hades, as well as a few glimpses of some story beats that take place in Quadratum, a realistic city inspired by modern-day Tokyo — an area that was also shown in the game's surprise trailer at the June 2026 Nintendo Direct.

This isn’t the last we’ll see of Kingdom Hearts IV this weekend; the game will also be discussed on August 15 in a panel titled ‘DEEP DIVE into KINGDOM HEARTS at D23,’ streaming at 4.30pm PT / 7.30pm ET / August 16 at 12.30 AM UK time. Disney has confirmed that it will feature a “behind-the-scenes look at the making of the games,” with names like Nana Gadd from Disney & Pixar Games, Tai Yasue from Square Enix, Haley Joel Osment, the voice of Sora, David Gallagher, the voice of Riku, and Renée Johnson, who voices some of the Disney-specific characters.

In the meantime, keep it locked to IGN for more news coming out of D23 this weekend, and check out everything that got announced at the event’s big presentation at the Honda Center on August 14.

items.title: First Trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter Shown at D23 — Here's What We Saw
items.description: Lucasfilm has shown off the debut trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter at the Disney fan event, D23.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Lucasfilm has shown off the debut trailer for Star Wars: Starfighter at the Disney fan event, D23.

The brief first look at the upcoming movie shows Ryan Gosling’s pilot character, now confirmed to be called Kade Auberon, discover a child playing with his decommissioned starfighter inside a garage. There's a reason it was decommissioned, Kade says. We then see Kade fly across a number of otherworldly landscapes, and in classic Star Wars fashion, droids shoot at the ship as Kade’s droid helps him escape.

On stage at D23, director Shawn Levy handed Gosling a new jacket to wear. On the back is the symbol of his character, Kade Auberon, which you can see below.

Starfighter is a standalone Star Wars movie that is neither a prequel nor a sequel, director Shawn Levy has insisted. "It’s a new adventure," he said of the post-Rise of Skywalker film at Star Wars Celebration 2025. "It’s set in a period of time that we haven’t seen explored yet." As part of that, it will not feature any "legacy characters," so don't expect to see Rey Skywalker pop up.

Ryan Gosling stars alongside Amy Adams, Aaron Pierre, Matt Smith, Mia Goth, and Flynn Gray. Star Wars: Starfighter is currently due to launch on May 28, 2027. Catch up on everything announced at D23 2026 right here.
